- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods to allow mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), apply a 3–5 period lagged decay to prevent overcorrection.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.6) and forecast diverges from history, favor smoother transitions — reduce volatility in forecast slope.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days), adjust forecast to align with recent 10–15 day average rather than full 30-day trend.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.5 → +0.3), apply a “sentiment momentum filter” — dampen forecast if sentiment shifts sharply within 3–5 days.
